extracted.intended_audience: NeurIPS 2024 attendees and the ML research community
extracted.subtask_description: Announcement of NeurIPS 2024 Best Paper Awards: four main-track papers (two best + two runner-up) and one Datasets & Benchmarks best paper. Each paper has a short committee rationale describing the underlying paper-quality properties (novelty, scalability, simplicity, presentation quality, opening new directions, societal value).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions based on scientific merit, blind to authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: The search committees considered all accepted NeurIPS papers equally, and made decisions independently based on the scientific merit of the papers, without making separate considerations on authorship or other factors, in keeping with the Neurips blind review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated meta-criterion for the Best Paper Award selection process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highly impactful papers selected from both tracks
rubrics_metrics.description: The best paper award committees were tasked with selecting a handful of highly impactful papers from both tracks of the conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel architecture that reframes a familiar problem
rubrics_metrics.description: This paper introduces a novel visual autoregressive (VAR) model that iteratively predicts the image at a next higher resolution, rather than a different patch in the image following an arbitrary ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best Paper main track (Visual Autoregressive Modeling). Praised for novelty: replacing arbitrary patch ordering with a principled next-scale prediction scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong empirical results and efficiency over prior methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The VAR model shows strong results in image generation, outperforming existing autoregressive models in efficiency and achieving competitive results with diffusion-based methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outperforms prior autoregressive methods in efficiency and matches diffusion-based methods in quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative core technical contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: At the core of this contribution lies an innovative multiscale VQ-VAE implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praised for a substantive technical innovation at the core of the method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall presentation quality, experimental validation, and insights
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall quality of the paper presentation, experimental validation and insights (scaling laws) give compelling reasons to experiment with this model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly enumerates presentation, experimental validation, and insights (scaling laws) as criteria the committee weighted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tractable solution to a previously intractable problem
rubrics_metrics.description: This paper proposes a tractable approach to train neural networks (NN) using supervision that incorporates higher-order derivatives. Such problems arise when training physics-informed NN to fit certain PDEs. Naive application of automatic differentiation rules are both inefficient and intractable in practice for higher orders k and high dimensions d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best Paper main track (Stochastic Taylor Derivative Estimator). Praised for tackling a regime previously considered intractable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method that addresses prior tradeoffs simultaneously
rubrics_metrics.description: While these costs can be mitigated independently (e.g. for large k but small d, or large d but small k using subsampling) this paper proposes a method, stochastic taylor derivative estimator (STDE) that can address both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praised for resolving a tradeoff that prior methods could only address one side of.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opens new directions in scientific applications
rubrics_metrics.description: This work opens up possibilities in scientific applications of NN and more generally in supervised training of NN using higher-order derivatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple method built on principled use of reference signals
rubrics_metrics.description: This paper presents a simple method to filter pre-training data when training large language models (LLM). The method builds on the availability of a high-quality reference dataset on which a reference language model is trained. That model is then used to assign a quality score for tokens that come from a larger pre-training corpus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Runner-up main track (Not All Tokens Are What You Need for Pretraining). Praised for simplicity and clean problem formulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensures training data quality alignment with reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Tokens whose scores have the highest rank are then used to guide the final LLM training, while the others are discarded. This ensures that the final LLM is trained on a higher quality dataset that is well aligned with the reference dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praised for an alignment-preserving filtering scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provides a practical alternative to a widely used technique
rubrics_metrics.description: This paper proposes an alternative to classifier free guidance (CFG) in the context of text-2-image (T2I) models. CFG is a guidance technique (a correction in diffusion trajectories) that is extensively used by practitioners to obtain better prompt alignment and higher-quality images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Runner-up main track (Guiding a Diffusion Model with a Bad Version of Itself). Praised for replacing a widely-used baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addresses a known empirical limitation of the baseline
rubrics_metrics.description: However, because CFG uses an unconditional term that is independent from the text prompt, CFG has been empirically observed to reduce diversity of image generation. The paper proposes to replace CFG by Autoguidance, which uses a noisier, less well-trained T2I diffusion model. This change leads to notable improvements in diversity and image quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praised for directly addressing a known limitation (diversity reduction) and producing notable improvements on both diversity and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addresses an impactful and topical research area
rubrics_metrics.description: Alignment of LLMs with human feedback is one of the most impactful research areas of today, with key challenges such as confounding by different preferences, values, or beliefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best Paper D&B track (PRISM Alignment Dataset). Framed as addressing one of today's most impactful research areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique perspective: subjective and multicultural feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: This paper introduces the PRISM dataset providing a unique perspective on human interactions with LLMs. The authors collected data from 75 countries with diverse demographics and sourced both subjective and multicultural perspectives benchmarking over 20 current state of the art models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praised for breadth of demographic coverage (75 countries), subjective + multicultural perspectives, and benchmarking against 20+ state-of-the-art models.

rubrics_metrics.name: High societal value and enabling future research
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper has high societal value and enables research on pluralism and disagreements in RLHF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites both intrinsic societal value and enabling-future-research as award rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse and ground-breaking contributions across tracks
rubrics_metrics.description: the best and runner up paper awards this year go to five ground-breaking papers (four main track and one datasets and benchmarks track) that highlight, respectively, a new autoregressive model for vision, new avenues for supervised learning using higher-order derivatives, improved training of LLMs and inference methods for text2image diffusion and a novel diverse benchmark dataset for LLM alignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meta-summary characterising the qualities valued across all award winners: 'ground-breaking', spanning new model architectures, new training paradigms, improved methodology, and novel benchmarks.
